faqs.question: Can you design my living room without a remodel?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most living room work is furniture, color, lighting, rugs, art and styling. We plan the layout, source the pieces, then install and style them. If you are changing a fireplace or adding built-ins, your contractor does that work.

faqs.question: How much does living room design cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on the scope, from a single consultation to full-service design. We quote after the discovery call. Our guide to [what an interior designer costs in Portland](/blog/interior-designer-cost-portland) explains how designers usually charge.

faqs.question: How far does a fireplace hearth need to extend?
faqs.answer: For a masonry fireplace, Oregon's 2023 residential code requires a hearth extension at least 16″ in front of the opening and 8″ past each side, or 20″ and 12″ when the opening is 6 sq ft or larger. Factory-built units follow their listing.

faqs.question: Can you work with furniture I already own?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can plan around the pieces you love and source what's missing. A few phone photos of the room and your furniture are a good start for the discovery call.

factChecks.quote: the clear width of walking surfaces shall be 36 inches (915 mm) minimum

factChecks.claim: Hearth extension 16″ in front, 8″ each side
factChecks.quote: Hearth extensions shall extend not less than 16 inches (406 mm) in front of and not less than 8 inches (203 mm) beyond each side of the fireplace opening.

factChecks.claim: Opening 6 sq ft or larger: 20″ in front, 12″ each side
factChecks.quote: Where the fireplace opening is 6 square feet (0.6 m 2 ) or larger, the hearth extension shall extend not less than 20 inches (508 mm) in front of and not less than 12 inches (305 mm) beyond each side of the fireplace opening.
The minimum thickness of hearth extensions shall be 2 inches (51 mm).

factChecks.claim: Combustible mantel or trim 6″ from opening
factChecks.quote: Exposed combustible mantels or trim is permitted to be placed directly on the masonry fireplace front surrounding the fireplace opening providing such combustible materials are not placed within 6 inches (152 mm) of a fireplace opening.
Combustible material within 12 inches (306 mm) of the fireplace opening shall not project more than 1 / 8 inch (3 mm) for each 1-inch (25 mm) distance from such an opening.
Hearth extensions of approved factory-built fireplaces shall be installed in accordance with the listing of the fireplace

factChecks.claim: 2023 ORSC still usable during the 2026 ORSC phase-in (mandatory April 1, 2027)
